parts: Please read the note /shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/notes/CHERN\_SIMONS\_WZW\_AND\_NATURAL\_LOEWNER\_EVOLUTION\_20260922. Please determine whether the proposed pilot is still the most worthwhile direction to pursue, and if so purse it.

I’ll read the note and the nearby research, assess whether the pilot still addresses a useful open question, and pursue it if the case holds up. I’ll save the assessment and any new results in the investigation.

The pilot still looks worthwhile for the physical question: WZW theory supplies a closed system of differential equations where the Yang–Mills approach still has an unresolved hierarchy. I’m narrowing it to SU(2) at level 2, with explicit boundary conditions and four spin-½ insertions, so the endpoint terms, initial state, and composition rule can all be calculated.

The calculation has produced a useful identity: after including the conformal factors, constant-driver evolution has a generator of the form \(-2Q^2/(k+2)\), with \(Q\) Hermitian for real boundary insertions. This gives a finite-dimensional norm-decrease identity. I’m checking it against the full four-point equations and testing how a moving driver changes the result.

The level-2 blocks also have explicit algebraic formulas, giving an independent check on the evolution. The moving-driver term can cause norm growth, so the contraction result has a precise restriction. I’ve also found that simply smearing this correlator cannot give the arithmetic transfer’s identity initial condition; the pilot is useful, but that later construction needs more than a four-point kernel.

The pilot is complete, and all 72 checks pass. The main result is a closed evolution with explicit blocks and sewing rules; the audit also distinguishes the fixed spin-tensor norm, which decreases for a constant driver, from the Chern–Simons gluing norm, which is preserved. I’m saving the derivation, reproducible checks, and a focused recommendation for the next calculation.

The next useful step is to study sewing on the full boundary Hilbert space, including descendants. This pilot now gives explicit formulas against which to check that construction. I’m preserving the manuscripts and saving the work as a research addendum with its limitations and internal audit.

Yes—the pilot remained the best next bounded physical calculation, and I completed it in SU(2) at level 2.

The [research note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/notes/SU2_LEVEL2_DETERMINISTIC_LOEWNER_PILOT_20260922.md) supplies explicit boundary conditions, four-point blocks, initial state, deterministic evolution, and gluing rules.

The main findings are:

- **Constant driving gives an exact norm-decrease identity** in the finite spin-tensor pairing.
- **Moving drivers can produce norm growth**, including for the physically selected initial block.
- **Chern–Simons gluing uses a different pairing.** Simply smearing the four-point correlator also fails to produce the arithmetic transfer’s identity initial condition.

All **72 checks passed**, including seven exact rational checks. An [internal audit](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/reviews/review_codex_wzw_loewner_pilot_20260922.md) records the assumptions and limitations.

The next worthwhile step is the actual slit-sewing operator on the full boundary Hilbert space, including descendants. The pilot now provides explicit formulas to test that construction. No arithmetic realization is claimed; existing manuscripts were preserved.
Before continuing, can you explain in what sense no arithmetic realization is claimed, and how the next steps will help move toward that goal?

By an **arithmetic realization**, I mean deriving the project’s specific shifted-zeta transfer \(V_{\omega,L}\) from independently defined physical observables. The pilot has not established that identification.

The required correspondence is quite restrictive. A physical boundary kernel \(K_t(x,y)\), acting on arbitrary boundary inputs, would need to satisfy

\[
K_0(x,y)=\delta(x-y),\qquad
\partial_tK_t
=-\dot\omega(t)\,G_{\omega(t),L}^{(x)}K_t.
\]

Here \(G_{\omega,L}\) is the **already specified arithmetic generator**. Its gamma contribution, pole contribution, local normalization, and prime-power translations must all emerge with their correct coefficients. The relationship between Loewner capacity \(t\) and arithmetic shift \(\omega\) also needs justification.

The pilot establishes a closed physical evolution, but several essential connections remain absent:

- Its propagator acts on two conformal-block components. Its identity initial condition is therefore an identity on that two-dimensional space.
- Smearing the four-point correlator produces a compact integral operator, whose initial kernel is not \(\delta(x-y)\).
- Its constant-driver norm-decrease identity uses a spin-tensor norm. We have not connected that norm to the boundary \(L^2\) norm needed for arithmetic positivity.
- There is no identified physical mechanism producing translations by \(\log n\) with the required prime-power weights.

The proposed sewing calculation would address the first layer of these problems. Sewing means composing physical regions by pairing their boundary states. Working with the full boundary Hilbert space, including descendants, could supply a genuine operator with a physically determined initial map, composition law, adjoint, and norm. The pilot’s explicit formulas would serve as checks on its primary-field matrix elements.

**Sewing alone would not explain the arithmetic.** I would therefore sharpen the next step into a bounded sequence:

1. **Construct the sewing operator and its boundary interpretation.** Determine whether physical preparation and readout can accommodate arbitrary spatial inputs with the required identity limit.
2. **Derive its spatial generator.** Test the arithmetic comparison first for \(L<\log 2\), where no prime-power translation occurs. This already requires the correct gamma, pole, and local terms.
3. **Cross the first prime threshold.** Determine whether the same construction independently produces translation by \(\log 2\) with the correct coefficient—and offers a rule extending to other prime powers.

My recommendation is strongest for understanding the physical Loewner evolution. Its value toward the arithmetic goal remains conditional on those comparisons. A failed comparison would be useful evidence to redirect the investigation; having more boundary states or a positive physical norm would not, by itself, establish the desired connection.

Is there any way to try to address the arithmetic realization more directly, perhaps by considering how the source of the arithmetic differential equation can be directly related to the Loewner evolution? If not, then please continue with the investigation.

I’ll examine how the arithmetic evolution equation is derived and whether that structure can connect directly to Loewner evolution. If it yields a sharper test than the proposed sewing calculation, I’ll pursue that first.

There is a more direct connection to test. The arithmetic generator comes from \(\xi'/\xi\); its zero expansion has the same Cauchy-kernel structure used in measure-driven Loewner equations. I’m checking whether this gives an actual geometric construction and where positivity would depend on an unproved RH-equivalent condition.

The connection is real, but it has an important limitation: using the unshifted \(\xi'/\xi\) as a positive Loewner driving function is already equivalent to RH. A sufficiently shifted version is valid unconditionally. I’m deriving that regularized construction and testing whether moving it toward zero shift gives a useful continuation method.

The direct construction passes the first checks: a shifted \(\xi'/\xi\) defines a valid Loewner flow and recovers the full arithmetic source, including the prime terms. I also found a useful obstruction: even under RH, the arithmetic shift generator itself need not have positive real part, so it cannot simply serve as the Loewner driving function. I’m recording both results to make the remaining gap precise.

The continuation question is now clearer. Moving farther right smooths the arithmetic source and preserves positivity; moving back toward the critical line reverses that process, and positivity can fail. An explicit model with zeros off the axis demonstrates the failure. The useful next target is therefore a cumulative norm identity for the arithmetic transfer, rather than positivity of its instantaneous generator.

The bounded investigation is complete: 60 checks passed, and the source construction, counterexamples, and internal audit are written. I also derived the operator bound available from the safe shift. Removing that shift introduces a factor \(e^{bL}\), so the bound does not establish contraction as the window grows. I’m saving the results and updating the research priorities.

**Yes—and I pursued that connection.** I now recommend it as the next focus for arithmetic matching.

Writing \(H(p)=\xi(\tfrac12+p)\), the arithmetic equation comes directly from
\[
m(p)=\frac{H'(p)}{H(p)},\qquad
\partial_\omega K_\omega(p)
=-[m(p-\omega)+m(p+\omega)]K_\omega(p).
\]

For a sufficiently large right shift, \(m(p+\eta)\) has positive real part. After normalization, it therefore defines a genuine generalized Loewner evolution. This incorporates the **complete arithmetic source**, including the gamma, rational, and prime terms. I also constructed a related flow along which \(\log H\) changes linearly with geometric time.

Two findings clarify the remaining problem:

- **Removing the shift is substantive.** Positivity of the unshifted source throughout the right half-plane is already equivalent to RH; the shifted construction cannot supply that conclusion automatically. This is a [classical positivity criterion](https://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/aa/aa89/aa8932.pdf).
- **The arithmetic generator cannot simply become the Loewner driver.** Even under RH, it has interior poles. An exact polynomial example also shows that a contractive cumulative transfer can have a generator with negative real part.

The next target is consequently a **boundary or canonical-system response realizing the cumulative transfer \(K_\omega\), with its correct unweighted norm**. The new construction supplies its arithmetic source; an independent realization must still explain the operator and positivity. I derived the weighted bound available immediately and identified precisely why it falls short.

Saved the [full investigation](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/notes/ARITHMETIC_SOURCE_AND_GENERALIZED_LOEWNER_EVOLUTION_20260922.md) and [internal audit](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/reviews/review_codex_arithmetic_loewner_source_20260922.md). **All 60 checks passed.**

Can you write up the current results into the folder /Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/WZW? I made this folder so that the manuscript in wilson-loewner wouldn't grow unreasonably long. I also made a notes folder within WZW for further investigation.
I’ll organize the WZW results and the arithmetic-source follow-up into a standalone write-up in the new folder, leaving the main Wilson–Loewner manuscript unchanged.

I’m using the PDF skill to prepare a standalone manuscript with editable source. It will cover the completed WZW pilot and the arithmetic-source connection, while the new `WZW/notes` folder will hold the continuation plan.

The write-up will distinguish three things throughout: decay in the fixed tensor norm, preservation of the Chern–Simons gluing norm, and the arithmetic operator norm that remains to be realized. I’ll keep the derivations self-contained and link the existing research notes and numerical records as provenance.

The manuscript is now 15 pages and builds successfully. It includes both result sets, their limitations, references, and the author and LLM acknowledgements. I’m checking the rendered pages and adding the build guide and continuation note before saving the package in `WZW`.

The new package links the original notes and numerical records, and gives future work its own home under `WZW/notes`. The page review caught a contents-page break and an awkward heading wrap; those are corrected. I’m finishing the visual check and recording the file identities for this delivery.
